Elevator feeder concept

A box of up to about 580 face-down cards on a floor that rises 0.31 mm (one card) at a time, so the top card always sits at the same height. A swappable head moves the top card's front edge into shared exit rollers. The pressing force on the card being fed stays the same from the first card to the last.

Concept model at real dimensions, for review before anything is printed. Parts are simplified (motors drawn as plain cylinders, no screws).

The card path, side cut

Heights in millimetres from the box base. This is the view that would have caught the 5 mm step on the old feeder: the card never drops, it climbs 2.6 mm over the separation ramp and enters the exit rollers just below that.

The top three cards clear the front wall; all three meet the rubber ramp, and only the top one is driven up it. That is how a paper tray's separation pad works. Its angle and grip are the first things to test.

Design check

  • ✓No height step. Top card 200.0, front wall 199.0, ramp end 202.6, nip 201.5 mm.
  • ✓The card is always driven. Its front edge reaches the exit rollers after 22.5 mm; the roller head keeps pushing until 70 mm, so there is overlap.
  • ✓Lift motor is strong enough. 580 cards weigh about 10 N; on an M8 threaded rod that takes about 0.007 N·m, and the 28BYJ-48 gives about 0.034. A fast T8 lead screw would need about 0.044, so it is the wrong choice here.
  • ✓Constant force. The card being fed carries its own weight (0.017 N) plus the roller's spring (set once, about 0.5–1 N), whether 5 or 580 cards are loaded.
  • ✓Fits the printer. The lower box is 170 mm tall (A1 mini limit 180) and 96 × 71 mm; the upper part is 36 mm.
  • ✓Loading. Lower the floor, flip the roller arm up on its pivot, drop the stack in.
  • ✗Found and fixed: flat 60 mm window tops would sag when printed (now peaked at 45°); the height switch was floating in the air (now on the pivot post).
  • !Capacity is about 580, not 600: the rising floor's guide skirts reach the box base. Shorter skirts would gain about 30 cards.
  • !Not detailed yet: how the two box parts screw together, the idler roller's spring, the pump and valve mounts, and the wiring (3 steppers use 12 GPIO pins; the Pi has enough).

Modules, parts and cost

Rough Korean online prices. The elevator and exit rollers are shared; the heads swap on the two rails along the top of the box.

Suggested build order

  1. Short test tower first. The upper box, the exit rollers and head A on a 60 mm lower box (about 150 cards). Proves pick, separation and exit for about 60 g of plastic instead of 200.
  2. Wear test on black-bordered cards (see the feeder options page) before trusting it with anything valuable.
  3. Head B on the same tower once A works, to compare.
  4. Full-height lower box (580 cards) once the top end is right.
